newsitem.title: USA: NORTHEASTERN STATES TO PETITION EPA ON SMOG - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: NORTHEASTERN STATES TO PETITION EPA ON SMOG - WSJ.

text.p: Some Northeastern states will soon petition the Environmental Protection Agency to crack down on Midwestern utilities in an attempt to cut the amount of wind-borne pollution that crosses state lines, the New York Times reported.
The states -- including Maine, Massachusetts and New York -- have agreed to a common legal strategy to press the EPA to act aggressively against the utilities, the paper said.
The states will ask the agency to impose limits on specific sources of polution, especially coal-fired electric utility plants, according to the paper.
The states hope to use their petitions -- filed through the Clean Air Act -- to emphasize the pollution from western utilities.
Northeastern officials said the move could save five years in eventually implementing controls on electric plants and other utilities in the western region, the paper said.
